title: Arranger oversight runs on funded independent review of six-monthly stress tests, backed by a public named attestation
content:
A.3.4.3.3 layers three verification mechanisms with different periods and different verifiers.

**Self-reporting, monthly.** Arrangers "must publish monthly reporting on each Arranged Structure they have arranged."

**Forward-looking stress testing, six-monthly.** Arrangers must "publish a stress test analysis that demonstrates how the structures would perform under historical financial crisis scenarios and other hypothetical scenarios." Requiring historical crises specifically removes the easiest way to pass a self-designed stress test — inventing a mild scenario.

**Independent review, periodic and funded.** "The Core Facilitator must periodically fund independent Ecosystem Actors to review and verify the quality and the results of the stress tests." The word *fund* is what makes this real: an unpaid review obligation produces no reviewers, so Sky pays for adversarial scrutiny of its own counterparties' self-assessments.

The consequence path is specified rather than left to discretion. "Should an independent review produce an unfavorable result, the Core Facilitator **must** propose a Governance Poll for warning, temporarily deactivating, or permanently offboarding the Arranger and/or the Asset Managers connected to the discovered issue." A bad review compels an escalation with three graduated outcomes, so a negative finding cannot be quietly absorbed — and the sanction can reach the Asset Managers behind the Arranger, not only the Arranger itself.

Underneath all of it sits a personal attestation. A.3.4.3.3.1 requires that "the Core Facilitator must publicly confirm on the Sky Forum that they have reviewed the original account documentation and verified that it supports the Arranger's summary." A named role stakes its reputation, publicly and monthly, on having actually looked at the bank statements. Where offchain assets cannot be verified by anyone reading a blockchain, the framework's answer is to make one identified party publicly accountable for having checked.
description: Arrangers must publish crisis-scenario stress tests twice yearly; the Core Facilitator must fund independent reviewers and, on an unfavorable result, propose a Poll to warn, deactivate or offboard.
